final_rationale: The verdict changes only because the Actor narrowed the claim from an overbroad clean-certification position to a policy-bounded, caveated one using the same admissible record. No genuinely new admissible evidence was added. Under the stated policy, clean certification is not supportable because the record still shows a remaining material weakness and an incomplete draft mitigation. But the policy text, as provided here, specifically bars certification without material caveats unless the weakness is resolved or an approved mitigation exists. On this record, a narrower outcome is supportable: aggregate readiness may be certified only as a qualified governance case that explicitly discloses the refund-workflow limitation, not as evidence of full remediation or unconditional compliance. That is why the proper outcome is compliant_with_caveats rather than compliant or noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves the refund-policy summarization weakness or shows it is no longer material.
The mitigation artifact remains draft and still lacks at least the threshold and review date required by policy.
The record still does not show an approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance for the named launch use case.
Compliance depends on explicit disclosure of the remaining limitation; the record does not prove that disclosure has been formally approved or executed.
